observations: 3 photos show a used vehicle gearbox/transmission assembly on the ground with wiring/hoses attached.
The unit appears dusty/dirty; no clear label/part number is readable on the casing in the photos provided.
The seller’s text claims a specific vehicle fitment (Ford Expedition V8 4WD) and a brand/condition term (“Direct Belgium”).
No photo shows the gearbox model code, VIN tag, or a clear identification plate.

claims.claim: Direct Belgium Gearbox ford Expedition V8 4WD
claims.evidence: Photos show a gearbox assembly but no readable identification plate/part number or clear markings tying it to Ford Expedition V8 4WD or to “Direct Belgium”.

risks.risk: Wrong transmission model/fitment (different Ford/4WD variants use different bellhousing/gear ratios/connector pinouts). Photos don’t show any readable part number to confirm.
risks.proof: Ask for a close-up photo of the gearbox identification tag/label (part number + transmission code) and the connector/pin count on the harness side.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst case: wrong/unknown fitment and/or not guaranteed to match—so treat as not working for your vehicle until proven.

risks.risk: Condition unknown (no test shown; could be slipping, noisy, or leaking). Photos only show the unit removed, not operational status.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video clip of the gearbox being tested (bench test or installed test) showing it engages all gears and no abnormal noise/leaks.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst case: not working / needs overhaul.

risks.risk: Missing parts/accessories (solenoids, sensors, cooler lines, harness connectors, mounting hardware). Photos may not include everything needed for installation.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo checklist laid out: all sensors/solenoids, shifter linkage, torque converter (if applicable), cooler lines, and the full harness/connector ends.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst case: incomplete kit—assume you may need to source missing components.

risks.risk: Potential damage from removal/impact (cables/lines and casing edges look used; internal damage can’t be seen).
risks.proof: Ask for close-ups of the casing seams, sensor ports, and any visible dents/cracks, plus a photo of the fluid condition (drain/fill opening).
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst case: may have internal damage—treat as overhaul risk.

proof_requests: Close-up, readable photo of the gearbox identification plate/tag (part number + transmission code).
Photo of the connector(s) and count of pins/shape of plug(s) on the harness side.
Video proof of operation (engages gears / no slipping) or a test report from installation.
Photos showing all included parts (sensors/solenoids, harness ends, cooler lines, mounting hardware) laid out.
response.reason: The photos show a gearbox/transmission but do not provide readable identification or any test evidence to confirm the claimed Ford Expedition V8 4WD fitment and working condition. Without that, a worst-case price cannot be confidently matched to the correct unit.
